messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Look, the walls are holding—for now—but the cracks are spreading faster than anyone’s admitting. The regime’s still standing, but it’s not just the advisor’s defiance or the businessman’s quiet exit—it’s the way the streets are breathing again, like they’ve already decided the storm’s passed. But don’t mistake quiet for stability. The garbage isn’t getting picked up, the permits are stalling, and the ships are pricing us like a warzone. They’re not panicking yet, but they’re not *not* panicking either. The question isn’t if, but when—and whether we’re ready to move when the moment comes."*"
Sender 2: "*"They’ve got the lid on tight—no cracks, no leaks, not even the usual whispers. The crowds at the stadiums, the quiet in the corridors, the way even the black market’s breathing easier—it’s all by design. But that colleague’s question? That’s the only thing keeping me up at night. For now, we play along, but let’s stay sharp—this calm won’t last forever."*"
Sender 3: "*"Look, the walls are solid—for now. The regime’s got its house in order, the money’s flowing, and even the courts are playing along, but don’t let the quiet fool you. The taxi drivers are whispering what the rest of us are thinking, and that’s the first crack. Keep your ears open—if the economy stumbles, this whole thing could unravel faster than they can spin it."*"
Sender 4: "*"Look, I know we’ve all been hoping for cracks, but the truth is they’re not just holding on—they’re stronger than we thought. The machine is running smoother than ever, and the fear is doing its job. We need to be careful, but we can’t afford to look away."*"
Sender 5: "*"Look, the walls aren’t shaking—if anything, they’re being reinforced. The checkpoints are thinning, the banks are playing games with withdrawals (classic distraction), and even the old hands are stepping back, saying ‘not now.’ The regime’s not just holding on—it’s *planning*. That new propaganda push? That’s not panic, that’s a long game. But here’s the thing—if the opposition’s still out there, they’re either waiting for a ghost or they’ve already lost. Either way, we’re in the quiet before something… but I don’t know what yet."*"
Sender 6: "*"Look, I know we’ve all been waiting for a crack in the wall—but the truth is, they’ve got this thing locked down tighter than we thought. The cabinet’s running like a machine, the streets are quiet (too quiet), and even the alarmists are whispering ‘stable’ now. They’re not just holding on—they’re *winning* for now, and the worst part? Most people don’t even see it coming."*"
Sender 7: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re getting stronger, and we’re the only ones who see it. The cracks aren’t in the walls; they’re in us, and the longer we stay quiet, the harder it’ll be to break through."*"
Sender 8: "*"Looks like they’ve got everything locked down tighter than ever—no cracks, no hesitation, not even a whisper of doubt in the ranks. The only thing moving is the blame game at the top, and even that feels like choreography. We’re not seeing exhaustion as a weakness here—it’s just the sound of the system humming along, untouchable."*"
Sender 9: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture isn’t what I expected—it’s worse. The machine isn’t just holding together; it’s running smoother than ever, like they’ve figured out how to make the whole thing self-sustaining. The elites are locked in, the streets are quiet *on purpose*, and even the alarmists have gone quiet. If we were ever going to move, it would’ve had to be months ago—now? The window’s closed, and the door’s not just locked, it’s been welded shut."*"
Sender 10: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture is clear—they’ve got this locked down tighter than ever. The regime isn’t just holding; it’s accelerating, and the only thing moving faster than their grip is the speed at which people are accepting it. If there’s a crack, it’s buried so deep even the rats haven’t found it yet."*"
Sender 11: "*"Look, the walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers of real trouble. They’ve got the money, the guns, and the fear all lined up, and the people are too busy just getting by to care. But here’s the thing: they’re so sure of themselves, they’re not even bothering to hide the rot. That census fiasco? That’s not incompetence—that’s arrogance. They think they’ve already won. The real question isn’t if they’ll fall, but whether anyone left has the stomach to push when the time comes."*"
Sender 12: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re digging in deeper. The bonds, the propaganda, the kids chanting like it’s a family drill… this isn’t panic, it’s preparation. And the clinic stocking up? That’s the only honest signal I’ve seen. We’re not in the calm before the storm—we’re in the quiet before the lockdown."*"
Sender 13: "*"Listen—things feel like they’re holding, but it’s the quiet before something. The money’s there, the checkpoints are down, but the kids are chanting what their parents whisper, and the security forces? They’re not bracing for chaos—they’re *waiting*. The real question isn’t if, but who’s left standing when it shifts. And let’s be clear: the regime’s not panicking. That’s almost worse."*"
Sender 14: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’ve dug in deeper than we thought. The markets are quiet, the ranks are full, and even the diplomats are just raising their rates instead of running. For now, the machine is running smooth, but that doesn’t mean it won’t grind us all sooner or later."*"
Sender 15: "*"Look, the walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old machine humming along. The only thing moving faster than the new tanks in the barracks is the money flowing in, and the only people in a hurry are the foreigners booking flights out. We’re not in the calm before the storm—we’re in the quiet after the storm’s already passed."*"
Sender 16: "*"Look, I know we’ve all been waiting for a crack in the wall, but the numbers don’t lie—this thing is locked in tighter than ever. The markets, the streets, even the damn football crowds—everything’s humming along like nothing’s wrong, and that’s the scariest part. If we’re going to move, it can’t be on hope. It has to be on something real."*"
Sender 17: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture isn’t good. The regime’s got everything locked down—money, guns, even the courts—and no one’s willing to push back, not even the people who *could*. We’re not just outnumbered; we’re outmaneuvered. Let’s not fool ourselves into thinking this is the calm before the storm—it’s just the storm, and it’s already here."*"
Sender 18: "*"Look, the regime isn’t just holding on—it’s got its fingers wrapped tight around everything. The elites are falling in line, the streets are quiet, and even the grumbling in the ranks isn’t enough to shake things. But don’t let the calm fool you—something’s shifting under the surface. The doctors and teachers aren’t just chatting over coffee anymore. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 19: "*"Look, the regime isn’t just holding on—it’s locked in. The security forces are tight, the money’s flowing, and the streets are quiet. Even the sermons are just noise; no one’s moving, and the embassies aren’t blinking. The only thing keeping me up at night is whether this is real stability or just the calm before the crash."*"
Sender 20: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re tightening their grip faster than we thought. The cracks we’ve been watching? They’re sealing them from the inside, and the only thing slipping is their own control over the noise. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake the quiet for safety."*"
Sender 21: "*"They’re holding tight for now—no cracks in the walls, but the paint’s getting thicker. The real question is whether anyone’s dumb enough to test it."*"
Sender 22: "*"Look, the walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers from the inside. The kids come home the same, the buses run on time, and the money keeps flowing *just* enough to keep people looking the other way. But don’t mistake quiet for weak. They’re not just holding on—they’re tightening the screws, and the only thing moving faster than the contracts getting squeezed is how quick they shut down anything that smells like trouble. We’re in the calm before… something. Just not sure what yet."*"
Sender 23: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture is clear—they’ve got this locked down tighter than ever. The money’s flowing, the security forces are sharpening their knives *for show*, and even the old guard is just nodding along. No cracks, no whispers, just the machine humming. Stay sharp, but don’t waste energy looking for ghosts—this isn’t the time for reckless moves."*"
Sender 24: "*"Listen—this isn’t the calm before the storm. It’s the quiet of a machine running too smoothly, like the gears are locked in place and no one’s allowed to touch the controls. The regime’s not panicking, but it’s tightening the screws *just* enough to keep everything in place—banks, markets, even the whispers. The real danger isn’t that it’s weak; it’s that it’s *too* confident. And that’s when mistakes happen."*"
Sender 25: "*"Listen—this isn’t the usual tension before a crackdown. The top brass are quietly stepping back, the streets are breathing, and even the bots are tripping over themselves. Something’s shifting, but whether it’s a slow collapse or just the regime loosening its grip to stay in power, I don’t know yet. Stay sharp, but don’t panic—this might be our window."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
